validation_against_experiment.value: Some difference exists between the experimental and CALPHAD-predicted phases; this was attributed to using the TCFE8 database instead of TCHEA3.

overall_structure.value: Multiphase structure: BCC (ferrite) as major phase together with partially ordered B2-type, γ-brass type and Fe5Si3-type silicide. At 800 °C no new phase change occurred relative to the milled powder but the amount of the B2-type phase increased.

source.reason: Overall phase constitution of the 800 °C annealed powder reported in the thermal-stability/annealing discussion and Table 4.

unmapped_findings: The 800 °C annealed specimen is a loose powder used to assess thermal stability / phase evolution; it was not consolidated by SPS, so the mechanical properties reported for the SPSed pellet (microhardness ~7.8 ± 0.3 GPa, elastic modulus 184 ± 5 GPa, compressive strength 2046 ± 160 MPa, ductility ~19%) do not apply to this sample state.
At 800 °C annealing, no new phase change occurred compared with the lower annealing temperatures, but the phase fraction of the B2-type phase increased (B2 = 40.00% at 800 °C).
Rietveld volumes of the 800 °C annealed phases (Table 4): BCC 23.39 Å³, γ-brass type 663.05 Å³, B2 24.13 Å³ and Fe5Si3 type 180.31 Å³.
The 35 h milled powder was annealed in a quartz tube back-filled with argon and then water quenched.
